newsitem.title: FRANCE: French 96 maize crop seen at 13.8 mln tonnes - AGPM.
newsitem.headline: French 96 maize crop seen at 13.8 mln tonnes - AGPM.

text.p: The French maize growers association AGPM expects the national maize crop to rise by one million tonnes to 13.8 million tonnes in 1996.
In its September newsletter, due for release later this week, AGPM is predicting the national yield may increase to some 8.0 tonnes per hectare from 7.7 tonnes last year.
France's farm ministry predicted in early August a 1996 maize crop of 13.7 million tonnes, assuming a yield of 7.88 tonnes per hectare and area of 1.734 million hectares.
AGPM said the ministry's yield estimate was "at the low end of a range whose high end could exceed 8.0 tonnes per hectare."

Noting yields in the main producing regions may reach and even break records, AGPM concluded that "the average yield could be at around 8.0 tonnes per hectare and production at around 13.8 million tonnes."
AGPM said yields in the Alsace region in eastern France could reach or even break the record 9.6 tonnes per hectare hit in 1990.
The Aquitaine and Midi-Pyrenees regions in the southwest and Rhone-Alpes may also meet or top their respective yield highs of 8.2 tonnes, 7.8 tonnes and 8.8 tonnes hit in 1993.
Steady rain has provided the crops in these regions with sufficient moisture but producers are voicing concern over the possible impact of recent cool temperatures.
In western France non-irrigated maize suffered from a prolonged spring drought but yields are forecast at around 5.8-6.0 tonnes in Brittany.
In centre France yields could reach 6.5-8.5 tonnes per hectare, depending on irrigation capacities.
The maize harvest is scheduled to start in mid-October but poor weather conditions could push it back.
